name: MIOSA

modes.label: Sandbox (fixed sizes xs-xl, managed)
modes.note: Hour = vCPU x $0.04536 + GB RAM x $0.01458 + sandbox disk GB x $0.0006147 (disk billed while running is folded into each size). Allocation billing, metered continuously, settled ~every 5 min; no rounding/minimum published. Sizes: xs 1/2/10, small 2/4/10 (default), medium 4/8/20, large 8/16/40, xl 16/32/80 (vCPU/GB/disk GB). timeout_sec max 86400; persistent sandboxes PAUSE at timeout (compute stops, disk moves to cold-storage rate). Re-checked 2026-09-28: 'Usage is metered continuously while a resource runs' (miosa.ai/pricing); idle_timeout_sec: 'Seconds without activity before auto-stop. `0`, the default, disables it.'; 'Persistent timeout pauses; non-persistent timeout destroys.' (miosa.ai/docs/api-reference/sandboxes). Allocation basis not stated verbatim (see caveat).

modes.label: Computer (durable Xfce desktop, fixed sizes)
modes.note: Same rate card as sandboxes but larger default disks (xs 10, small 20, medium 50, large 100, xl 200 GB), which bill at $0.0006147/GB-h while running. Page calculator check: 2 vCPU + 4 GB + 20 GB = 16.13 credits/h = $0.1613/h. Stopped computers bill disk at cold-storage rate ("or charges at the stopped rate, depending on your plan").

modes.label: Bring your own cloud (45% orchestration fee only, + your cloud bill)
modes.note: MIOSA charges 45% of the managed rate (vCPU $0.0204, RAM $0.006561/GB-h, disk running $0.00027662/GB-h, cold $0.00001094/GB-h, egress $0.0225/GB, GPU $0.7875/h); your AWS/GCP/Azure bill for the same resources is NOT included, so this mode understates total cost. BYOC is a gated private preview needing /dev/kvm hosts.

plans.name: Developer
plans.note: $10 one-time credit (1,000 credits), no card to start; hard stop at $0 (no overage, no auto-recharge) until a card is added. 3 Computers / 10 Sandboxes / 2 concurrent workloads. 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 10 GB per-computer cap was on the page earlier on 2026-09-28 but is gone from the live page on re-check.

plans.name: Business
plans.note: $500/month minimum spend credited 1:1 as 50,000 credits; overage with spend controls; top-ups $1-$5,000 at the same rate. 100 Computers / 250 Sandboxes / 50 concurrent. Per-computer cap 8 vCPU/16 GB/40 GB (earlier capture; removed from live page). Docs also say 10 concurrent sandboxes per tenant by default (raise via support). Cancellation at end of billing period.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: $1,000/month minimum credited 1:1 (100,000 credits); same rates; SSO/SCIM, dedicated support; "Request Enterprise", cancellation per agreement. 200 Computers / 500 Sandboxes / 200 concurrent.

extras.price: $1.75/GPU-hour on the rate card (type unspecified); managed GPU sandboxes not shipped yet (planned)

perf_source: computesdk: burst_tti median 361.21 ms at 100 concurrent (2026-09-25), DAX total 38.84 s (2026-09-25, 8 vCPU / 15.6 GiB x86_64 env). No computesdk cold_start_tti row and no hpc CPU run.
caveats: Rates are exact credit prices (1 credit = $0.01): vCPU 4.536, RAM 1.458/GB-h, disk running 0.06147/GB-h, cold storage 0.00243/GB-h, egress 5/GB. Page rounds vCPU to $0.0454 and RAM to $0.0146.

Disk-while-running is folded into each size hour; while paused/stopped the disk bills at cold-storage $0.01774/GB-month (encoded as snapshot_gib_month). Whether a paused memory image adds to the GB counted is unpublished.
Per-computer plan caps (Dev 2/4/10, Business 8/16/40, Enterprise 16/32/80) were on the pricing page earlier on 2026-09-28 and are absent on re-check; kept in plans as they may still be enforced.

Stale conflicting docs: /docs/api-reference/credits still lists an old model (Small 4GB/1CPU 3 credits/h, Medium 6, Large 12; plans Free/Starter $29/Pro $79/Scale $199; credits expire 180 days). Ignored in favour of the pricing page.
Plan fee = monthly minimum credited 1:1, so Business/Enterprise cost max(fee, usage).
Docs: default 10 concurrent sandboxes per tenant (raise via support) vs. plan pages 2/50/200 concurrent workloads.
Billing granularity/minimum unpublished (metered continuously, ledger settles ~5 min). GB vs GiB not specified (page says GB).
BYOC mode excludes the underlying cloud bill; gated private preview. GPU rate $1.75/h is on the card but managed GPU is not shipped.
Regions: 3 US regions (us-west-la, us-east-ny, us-mia), no multiplier.

unverified: may bill active CPU/RAM rather than allocation. The pricing page lists per-vCPU-h / per-GB-h rates metered 'while a resource runs' without saying allocated vs used; the sandbox usage endpoint 'Returns measured runtime, provisioned vCPU time, active CPU, network traffic, estimated cost' (miosa.ai/docs/api-reference/sandboxes). Card keeps allocation (checked 2026-09-28).
Idle auto-stop exists but is opt-in: idle_timeout_sec defaults to 0 (disabled); timeout_sec defaults to 3600 s (max 86400).
Idle auto-stop exists but is off by default (must be configured), so the estimator does not apply idle suspension; set a pinned offer if you enable it.

BYOC is fee-only + your cloud bill: "Your cloud provider bills you directly for the underlying compute, storage, and network — MIOSA only charges for orchestrating it, at 45% of the managed rate" (miosa.ai/pricing, 2026-09-28). Its row is the orchestration fee alone, flagged alt; add the AWS/GCP/Azure cost of the same VM.

Disk is not sold separately for sandboxes: disk_size_mb "must match the selected canonical size" (miosa.ai/docs/api-reference/sandboxes, 2026-09-28); each size carries a fixed disk (sandbox medium 20 GB, Computer medium 50 GB) billed at 0.06147 credits/GB-h while running, folded into the size price. A bigger disk means a bigger size or a Computer, so disk_gib_month stays null.

fleet.verification: Developer no card for introductory credit; card to continue. Paid minimums become usage credit when payment clears.
fleet.tiers: Developer 2 active workloads, 3 retained Computers/10 Sandboxes; Business 50 active, 100/250 retained; Enterprise 200 active, 200/500 retained.
fleet.notes: Concurrency is separate from retained counts. 10/50 require Business ($500 monthly minimum becomes credit); Enterprise $1,000 minimum requires request. 300/1,000 not a published entitlement.

snapshot_auto.quote: Stopping a computer pauses billing (or charges at the stopped rate, depending on your plan). Restarting resumes from the snapshot.
snapshot_auto.note: Triggers: Computer stop and inactivity auto-stop ('auto_stop_seconds': 'Seconds of inactivity before auto-stop', /docs/api-reference/computers); for Sandboxes, 'Persistent timeout pauses; non-persistent timeout destroys' and idle_timeout_sec auto-stop (default 0 = off), with pause described as 'snapshot-backed' (/docs/develop/snapshots). Memory: Computer snapshots capture 'CPU state, RAM, and filesystem', so resume-from-snapshot likely restores processes, but the stop/pause pages only promise 'filesystem state is preserved' / 'suspends guest vCPU execution ... while preserving its workspace'. Treat memory retention on auto-stop as unconfirmed.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Snapshots capture the full in-memory state of a running computer - CPU state, RAM, and filesystem - and store it durably. Restore a snapshot to spin up an identical computer in seconds.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Computers: POST /computers/{id}/snapshots (running only), restore creates a new computer; 'Snapshot-based parallelism (clone a baseline)' recipe restores N workers. Sandboxes: POST /sandboxes/{id}/fork 'creates a new sandbox from a copy-on-write snapshot of a running sandbox'; /docs/develop/snapshots also lists CLI 'miosa sandbox snapshot' + 'miosa sandbox create --snapshot', but /docs/known-limitations says 'Standalone snapshot management is not in canonical public V1' (contradictory docs; fork is the stable sandbox path). Memory included; new machines can boot from it.

harness_api.quote: Agent Runs are the prompt-dispatch interface for MIOSA sandboxes and computers. Use them when your product needs to send a natural-language task into a device, run it through OSA, Codex, Claude Code, Pi, Hermes, or a custom runtime, and receive a stable run response your UI can render.
harness_api.note: POST /api/v1/agent-runs (provider: osa, codex, claude/claude-code, pi, hermes, custom), durable events + SSE stream (GET /agent-runs/{id}/events?stream=true), cancel, artifacts, Agent Run Groups for multi-agent orchestration, runtime profiles; CLI 'miosa agent run --sandbox/--computer', 'miosa sandbox prompt'. Runtime-routing guide also lists Gemini CLI / OpenCode as customer-provided runtimes. No documented follow-up/resume-conversation endpoint; each run is a prompt dispatch.

egress_allowlist.quote: Pattern kinds: exact (literal host), wildcard (*.example.com), cidr (IP literal targets only).
egress_allowlist.note: Egress policies per Computer/Sandbox with mode audit_only/enforce and default_action allow/deny ('Tenant default starts in audit_only mode'), enforced by the host-side proxy. Computers additionally have /computers/{id}/network-policy with modes unrestricted/allowlist/denylist/isolated, host+port+protocol rules: 'Network policies apply at the microVM level.' Allowlist suggestions from the audit log.

egress_http_rules.note: Allowlist rules carry method and path_glob in addition to host; warn_only and priority fields. No header-level rules documented. Audit log records method/path per request.

ingress_rules.quote: Requires either an authenticated MIOSA session OR a valid share token.
ingress_rules.note: Preview URLs per port ({port}-{slug}.sandbox.miosa.ai) with public/private visibility, short-lived share tokens (preview_token, stripped by the proxy), preview tokens for iframes, custom preview domains. No IP allowlist documented.

guest_firewall.note: Firecracker microVM ('isolated microVM workspaces', /docs/api-reference/sandboxes) with root (exec default cwd /root, sudo apt-get in examples); nftables/iptables inside not documented.

secret_proxy.quote: the MIOSA proxy on your VM’s host sees the request, finds miosa-tok-7f2a8c1d4b2e6f0a in the Authorization header, and swaps it with your real sk-proj-... before forwarding to OpenAI. OpenAI sees the real key. Your sandbox never did.
secret_proxy.note: Any API key (example uses OpenAI and Stripe), plus OAuth Connect tokens with auto-refresh; placeholder swapped in headers, query params, URL paths and buffered bodies; rotation without restart; 5 scope levels; per-request audit. Docs claim it works with 'curl, requests, fetch, axios, gRPC' at the network layer; databases/SSH/git-over-SSH not mentioned. Per-secret host binding (which destinations may receive the real value) not documented.

volume_attach.quote: Create a persistent block device, attach it to a compatible computer on the same host, and preserve writes independently of the computer lifecycle.
volume_attach.note: Computers (and App Engine runtime instances); local-backend ext4, max 500 GB, 10 per project, host-bound ('Cross-host attach returns a clear error'). /docs/known-limitations still labels Volumes 'Beta'. Not documented for Sandboxes.
